newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai soymeal firms, feedmillers delay imports.
newsitem.headline: Thai soymeal firms, feedmillers delay imports.

text.p: Thai soymeal prices rose as feedmillers delayed importing in hopes the caretaker government would lift import quotas or cut import tariffs on feed raw materials, trade and industry sources said on Wednesday.
Expectations that soymeal prices would drop further on bullish soybean supply prospects due to good weather also encouraged them to take a wait-and-see stance, they added.
The price of local soymeal from imported soybeans was quoted at around 10.45 baht per kg (US$0.42) from 10.30-10.40 a kg last week.

The only import order confirmed by trade sources was the one made last week by a major local feed producer, who bought 15,000 tonnes of soybean from the United States for October shipment. The price was said to be US$335 per tonne C&F Bangkok.
"Besides that, we heard nothing. That's why the local soymeal prices continue to rise," said one trader.

Although the industry is facing a supply shortage, impending arrival of U.S. corn gluten meal by next week and cargoes of soymeal from Brazil and Argentina later this month would give feed producers some room to wait, they said.
The shortage was also alleviated partly by easing prices of fishmeal that could be a substitute for soymeal.

"The Commerce Ministry already agreed with us that it would be in the country's best interest to lift the import quota," said Chevee Visej, a manager for the Thai Soymeal Trader and Importer Association.
"Or at least cut import tariffs. That's what the government should do before the general election is held in November," he said.
Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa dissolved the parliament on Friday. A general election will be held on November 17.
Corn/maize prices, meanwhile, were stable to lower as the industry awaited fresh supply from the the second crop.
The prices of silo grade corn were quoted at 4.25-4.30 baht a kg from 4.30-4.50 baht a kg last week. Feed grade corn was quoted at 4.60 baht a kg, barely changed from last week.
